newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on speculation, defies peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on speculation, defies peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 70 basis points at 22.70 percent on Friday after the market gave way to speculation despite the peso getting back on its feet, traders said.
"Dealers suddenly placed higher and higher rates in their orders to buy, even though the peso had already begun to recover," a dealer said.
"There was plenty of both money and paper out there, so it was a case of seeing who blinked first," he added.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 25 basis points at 23.50 percent.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended 3.4 centavos firmer at 7.9400/7.9460 per dollar.
Traders said the recovery came in the wake of an excessive run on the peso during trade on Thursday.
Dealers pointed out that rates in the term market declined despite the gain on overnight government paper.
"The term market was much calmer. Traders bought ahead of (U.S. President) Clinton certifying Mexico, and a firmer peso poured cold water on jitters," another trader said.
U.S. government officials announced during late trade in that Mexico had received recertification as a drug-war ally.
Secondary rates on 182-day Cetes closed down 20 basis points at 23.00 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 528 million pesos into the system by auctioning a three-day credit, which it assigned at 20.85 percent.
Liquidity of 5.288 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system, but demand for cash to meet payroll expenses and for the weekend drained a lot of liquidity from the market, traders said.
Dealers said a weaker peso and higher secondary money market rates clearly paved the way for primary rates to increase at next week's primary auction.
"Although we expect a much more relaxed market on Monday, primary rates have obviously reached rock bottom and are on the rebound," a money market analyst said.
Liquidity of 400 million pesos is scheduled to return to the system on Monday.
